item.content:encoded:
How did you know I was a smug killjoy?
Of COURSE I have had experiences like this, thoroughly creepy things that have happened. I don't understand how explaining these things degrades the story or the enjoyment of it- just thinking about these experiences still send chills down my spine. And I did admit the cat was creepy, as well. As for the eight years ago bit, I just comment on whatever interests me, regardless of age.
I thoroughly apologize if my tone offended you or anybody else. I was just stating some facts that I had observed over the course of the story.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It was a white Japanese Bobtail. They have barely any tail, so much so that it sometimes looks like they don't have one.
And it also sounds like the cat was slightly on edge a lot. When cats are on edge, they make that increasingly louder "mmmmMMMMMRMRRRAAAAA" sound. My grandma had a cat that would beep like a freaking alarm clock when my poor uncle came around.
I can't quite explain the toothless mouth, but I HAVE seen cats open their mouths at angles where the teeth are not visible.
Your demoncat is somewhat boring and mundane, not a living SCP. Sorry.
EDIT- I DO concur, however, that cats can be really freaky when they want to be. My uncle's, totally unrelated, cat, hides in the closet all day making snake noises and startling anyone who passes by with its glowing gold eyes. +1

item.content:encoded:
I read this story several months back. It gave me the heebie-jeebies like I can't describe and I was distinctly uncomfortable around my girlfriends cat for the next few days. I got over it and haven't thought about the story since. Until last night when we are having dinner at her parents house to celebrate her birthday. In the middle of a nice piece of cake, I hear a perfectly ordinary #meow#, fall out of my chair and nearly die. That is not hyperbole. My whole body jerked with immediate terror, my chair fell backwards and I choked on my dessert. Her brother had to give me the heimlich.

Congratulations, Yoric, you have given me permanent cat-o-phobia. I'm sending you my therapy bills.

item.content:encoded: I felt a chill through most of that, although I have to say it was the conclusion there that really got me. Yoric almost being eaten by Fluffy Satan is unnerving and scary in its own right, but the thought about everyone filtering out the horrors of the world stretches that out to a way that it can be anywhere. That homeless man on the corner, the one in the jacket? Come to think of it, you can't really think and describe to well what that jacket is like. Hell, you're not sure he even looks homeless, you just assume that. He's always there. That must be what he is….
